Ibn Adi and Ibn Asakir transmitted from Aishah concerning His words: ﴿And when the Prophet confided a matter to one of his wives, a saying﴾, she said: "He confided to her that Abu Bakr is my successor after me."

Ibn Adi, Abu Nu'aym in al-Sahabah, al-Ushari in Fada'il al-Siddiq, Ibn Mardawayh, and Ibn Asakir transmitted through routes from Ali and Ibn Abbas, who said: "By God, the governance of Abu Bakr and Umar is in the Book: ﴿And when the Prophet confided a matter to one of his wives, a saying﴾. He said to Hafsah: 'Your father and the father of Aishah will govern the people after me, so beware of informing anyone of this.'"

I say: this does not state that it was the occasion of revelation of His words ﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you?﴾. Rather, it states that the matter which the Messenger of God (ﷺ) confided was this.

Even if it were granted that it has a chain fit to be considered, it is opposed by those authentic narrations that have preceded it, and those are given precedence over it and are preferred to it.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn Abbas concerning His words ﴿Your hearts have certainly swerved﴾, he said: "they deviated and sinned."

Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from him that he said: "they inclined."

Ibn Asakir transmitted through the route of Abd Allah ibn Buraydah, from his father, concerning His words ﴿and the righteous among the believers﴾, that he said: "Abu Bakr and Umar."

Ibn Asakir transmitted from Ibn Mas'ud something similar.

Al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and Abu Nu'aym in Fada'il al-Sahabah transmitted through another route from him something similar.

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn Umar and Ibn Abbas something similar.

Al-Hakim transmitted from Abu Umamah, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ), something similar.

Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted, al-Suyuti said with a weak chain, from Ali, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "It is Ali ibn Abi Talib."

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted "from Asma' bint Umays: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: ﴿and the righteous among the believers﴾ is Ali ibn Abi Talib."

Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Asakir transmitted from Ibn Abbas concerning His words ﴿and the righteous among the believers﴾ that he said: "It is Ali ibn Abi Talib."

Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Buraydah concerning His words ﴿previously married and virgins﴾, that he said: "God promised His Prophet (ﷺ) in this verse that He would marry him to the previously married Asiyah, the wife of Pharaoh, and to the virgin Maryam bint Imran."

Surah 66 (Al-Tahrim)

It is Madinan (revealed at Madinah).

Al-Qurtubi said: this is the consensus (fi qawl al-jami'), and it is also called "Surat al-Nabi" (the Surah of the Prophet).

Ibn al-Durays, al-Nahhas and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Surat al-Tahrim was revealed at Madinah." The wording of Ibn Mardawayh is "Surat al-Muharram."

Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Ibn al-Zubayr, who said: "Surat al-Nisa' was revealed at Madinah," [meaning] ﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid [yourself] what Allah has made lawful for you?﴾ — i.e., Surat al-Tahrim.

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

His saying: ﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you?﴾ Scholars differed about the occasion of revelation of this verse, in several reports. The first is the view of most of the exegetes.

Al-Wahidi said: The exegetes said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) was in the house of Hafsah, and she went to visit her father. When she returned, she saw Mariyah in her house with the Prophet (ﷺ). She did not enter until Mariyah had left, then she entered. When the Prophet (ﷺ) saw jealousy and displeasure on Hafsah's face, he said to her: 'Do not tell 'A'ishah, and I promise you that I will never approach her again.' Hafsah told 'A'ishah, and they were close friends. 'A'ishah became angry and kept at the Prophet (ﷺ) until he swore that he would not approach Mariyah. So Allah revealed this surah."

Al-Qurtubi said: Most of the exegetes hold that the verse was revealed concerning Hafsah, and he mentioned the story.

It was also said that the cause was that "he (ﷺ) used to drink honey at the house of Zaynab bint Jahsh, so 'A'ishah and Hafsah agreed that when he came to them they would say to him, 'We smell maghafir (a foul odour) from you.'"

It was also said that the cause was the woman who gave herself to the Prophet (ﷺ).

The evidence for these reports will come at the end of the discussion, God willing, and you will learn how to reconcile them.

The clause ﴿seeking the pleasure of your wives﴾ is either a new (independent) sentence, or it explains the word "tuharrimu" (you forbid), or it is in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal) from the subject of "tuharrimu," meaning: seeking by it the pleasure of your wives. "Mardat" (pleasure) is a verbal noun (ism masdar), and its root is "mardawah." It is in construct with the object, meaning: that you please your wives; or with the subject, meaning: that they be pleased. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving, Merciful﴾, i.e., abundant in forgiveness and mercy for what has passed from you of forbidding what Allah made lawful for you. It was said: this was a minor sin, and therefore Allah rebuked him for it. It was also said: it is a rebuke for leaving what is better (tark al-awla).

﴿Allah has already ordained for you the dissolution of your oaths﴾, i.e., He prescribed for you the release from your oaths and explained that to you. "Tahillah" originally was "tahlilah," and it was assimilated (idghām).

It is a verbal noun of the form "tafil," like "tawsiyah" and "tasmiyah." So the oath is regarded as a binding, and expiation is a release, because it releases the one who swore from what he forbade upon himself.

Muqatil said: the meaning is: Allah has explained the expiation of your oaths in Surat al-Ma'idah.

Allah commanded His Prophet (ﷺ) to expiate his oath and to resume relations with his slave-girl, and he freed a slave.

Al-Zajjaj said: No one has the right to forbid what Allah has made lawful.

I say: This is the truth, that the forbidding of what Allah has made lawful does not take effect and does not bind the one who says it.

Thus permitting and forbidding belong to Allah, Glorified is He, and not to anyone else, and His rebuke of His Prophet (ﷺ) in this surah is the most eloquent proof of that. The discussion is lengthy, the positions on it are many, and the discourses on it are extensive; we have verified it in our works sufficiently.

The scholars differed over whether mere forbidding (tahrim) constitutes an oath that requires expiation or not, and there is disagreement on this. There is nothing in the verse that indicates it is an oath, because Allah rebuked him for forbidding what He had made lawful for him, then said: ﴿Allah has already ordained for you the dissolution of your oaths﴾. It is reported in the story which most exegetes consider the cause of revelation, that he first forbade, then swore a second time, as we have mentioned. ﴿And Allah is your Protector (mawlakum)﴾, i.e., your Guardian, your Helper, and the One who manages your affairs. ﴿And He is the All-Knowing﴾ of what is good for you and your success, ﴿the All-Wise﴾ in His actions and His words.

﴿And when the Prophet confided to one of his wives a statement﴾. Most exegetes said: she was Hafsah, as already mentioned, and the statement was the forbidding of Mariyah, or the honey, or the forbidding of the woman who gave herself to him. The adverbial element (zarf) is governed by an implied verb, meaning: "Remember when he confided."

Al-Kalbi said: He confided to her that your father and the father of 'A'ishah would be the successors over my community after me. ﴿And when she informed [another] of it﴾, i.e., she told someone else. ﴿And Allah made him aware of it﴾, i.e., Allah informed His Prophet of that actual disclosure she made to others. ﴿He made known part of it﴾, i.e., he informed Hafsah of part of what she had disclosed.

The majority read "'arrafa" with the doubled letter, from "ta'rif" (making known). 'Ali, Talhah ibn Musarrif, Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, al-Hasan, Qatadah and al-Kisa'i read it without doubling. Abu 'Ubayd and Abu Hatim preferred the first reading, because of His saying: ﴿and he turned away from part of it﴾, i.e., he did not make it known to her. Had it been unstressed, he would have said in its opposite: "and denied part." ﴿And he turned away from part﴾, i.e., he turned away from making known part of that, out of disliking that it spread among the people. It was also said: what he turned away from was the story of Mariyah.

There is much confusion among the exegetes here, and each group interpreted "ta'rif" and "i'rad" in a way that matches some of the reports on the occasion of revelation. We will clarify this for you, God willing.

﴿So when he informed her of it﴾, i.e., he told her what she had spread of the statement. ﴿She said: "Who told you this?"﴾, i.e., who informed you of it. ﴿He said: "The All-Knowing, the All-Aware informed me"﴾, i.e., He Who nothing is hidden from informed me.

﴿If you two turn in repentance to Allah, your hearts have certainly inclined﴾. The address is to 'A'ishah and Hafsah, i.e., if you two repent to Allah, then there has occurred from you both what requires repentance. The meaning of "sagha" is: they deviated and turned away from the truth, namely that they loved what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) disliked, which is the spreading of the statement.

It was also said: the meaning is: if you two turn in repentance to Allah, your hearts have indeed inclined toward repentance. He said "qulubukuma" (your hearts) and not "qalbakuma" (your two hearts), because the Arabs dislike combining two dual forms in one expression. ﴿And if you band together against him﴾, i.e., "tatazahara." The majority read "tazaharaa" with one of the two tas elided for lightness. 'Ikrimah read "tatazaharaa" in its original form. al-Hasan, Abu Raja', Nafi' and 'Asim in one narration read "tazzahharaa" with doubled za and ha, without alif. The meaning of "tazahur" is mutual support and cooperation; the sense is: if you two support and cooperate with each other in jealousy over him and in disclosing his secret. ﴿Then indeed Allah is his Protector, and Jibril and the righteous among the believers﴾, i.e., Allah takes charge of his support, and likewise Jibril and whoever of His righteous servants among the believers; so he will never lack a helper who supports him. ﴿And after that, the angels are a supporting company﴾, i.e., after Allah's support of him, and the support of Jibril and the righteous believers, the angels are helpers who back him. "Al-Malaikah" is the subject, and "zahir" is its predicate.

Abu 'Ali al-Farisi said: the form "fa'il" has come for plurality, as in His saying: ﴿and no intimate friend will ask after an intimate friend﴾ [al-Ma'arij: 10]. Al-Wahidi said: this is a singular that stands for the plural, like His saying: ﴿and excellent are those as companions﴾ [al-Nisa': 69]. It is established in the science of grammar that words like "jarih," "sabur," and "zahir" are applied to the singular, the dual, and the plural.

It was also said: the mutual support between 'A'ishah and Hafsah was in trying to control the Prophet (ﷺ) regarding maintenance (nafaqah).

﴿Perhaps his Lord, if he divorces you, will substitute for him wives better than you﴾, i.e., He will give him in your place wives better than you. Allah, Glorified is He, knew that he would not divorce them, but He informed of His power, that if divorce occurred from him, He would replace them with better than them, as a warning to them. This is like His saying: ﴿and if you turn away, He will replace you with another people other than you﴾ [Muhammad: 38], for it is a report about power and a warning to them.

Then He described the wives with His saying: ﴿submissive, believing﴾, i.e., those who uphold the obligations of Islam, affirming Allah, His angels, His books, His messengers, and the decree, both its good and its evil.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: ﴿submissive﴾ means sincere (mukhlisat). It was also said: its meaning is those who submit to the command of Allah and His Messenger. ﴿Devout﴾, obedient to Allah. Qunut is obedience; it was also said: ones who pray. ﴿Repentant﴾, i.e., from sins. ﴿Worshipful﴾ to Allah, humbled before Him.

Al-Hasan and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: ones who worship abundantly. ﴿Wandering (sa'ihat)﴾, i.e., fasting.

Zayd ibn Aslam said: emigrants (muhajirat), and there is no wandering (siyahah) in the community of Muhammad (ﷺ) except hijrah.

Ibn Qutaybah, al-Farra' and others said: fasting was called siyahah because the wanderer has no provision with him.

It was also said: the meaning is those who go forth in obedience to Allah, from "sa'a al-ma'" (the water flowed) when it departs. The root of siyahah is roaming on the earth. The discussion of siyahah has already passed in Surat Bara'ah. ﴿Previously married and virgins﴾: He placed the conjunction between them because they are contrary to each other. "Thayyibat" is the plural of "thayyib," a woman who has been married and then separated from her husband, returning to the state of one without a husband.

"Abkar" is the plural of "bikr," a virgin, named so because she remains in the original state in which she was created.

Al-Bukhari and others narrated from 'A'ishah that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to remain with Zaynab bint Jahsh and drink milk or honey with her. So I and Hafsah agreed that whichever of us the Prophet (ﷺ) entered upon, she should say: "I smell maghafir from you." He entered upon one of them and she said that to him. He said: "No, rather I drank honey at the house of Zaynab bint Jahsh, and I will never return to it." Then the verse was revealed: ﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid what Allah has made lawful for you?﴾ up to His saying: ﴿If you two turn in repentance to Allah﴾ addressed to 'A'ishah and Hafsah, and ﴿And when the Prophet confided to one of his wives a statement﴾ refers to his saying: "No, rather I drank honey."

Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh narrated, and al-Suyuti said with a sound chain, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) drank a drink of honey at the house of Sawda. He entered upon 'A'ishah, and she said: 'I smell a scent from you.' He entered upon Hafsah, and she said: 'I smell a scent from you.' He said: 'I think it is from a drink I drank at the house of Sawda. By Allah, I will never drink it again.' So Allah revealed: ﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid...﴾ the verse."

Ibn Sa'd narrated from 'Abd Allah ibn Rafi' who said: "I asked Umm Salamah about this verse, ﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid...﴾. She said: 'I had a jar of white honey, and the Prophet (ﷺ) used to lick from it, and he loved it. 'A'ishah said to him: "Its bees graze on 'urfut (a bitter plant), so he forbade it," and the verse was revealed.'"

al-Nasa'i and al-Hakim (who authenticated it) and Ibn Mardawayh narrated from Anas: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had a slave-girl with whom he had relations, until 'A'ishah and Hafsah kept at him until he made her forbidden to himself," and Allah revealed this verse: ﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid...﴾.

al-Bazzar and al-Tabarani narrated, and al-Suyuti said with a sound chain, from Ibn 'Abbas who said: "I asked 'Umar ibn al-Khattab: 'Who are the two women who backed each other up?' He said: ''A'ishah and Hafsah.' The beginning of the matter concerned Mariyah the Copt, mother of Ibrahim, whom the Prophet (ﷺ) had relations with in Hafsah's house on her day. Hafsah became upset and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, you have done with me something you have not done with any of your wives, on my day and on my bed.' He said: 'Are you not pleased that I forbid her to myself and never approach her again?' She said: 'Yes.' So he forbade her and said: 'Do not mention this to anyone.' But she mentioned it to 'A'ishah, and Allah made him aware of it, and Allah revealed: ﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid...﴾ all the verses. We were told that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) expiated for his oath and [afterward] had relations with Mariyah."

Ibn Sa'd and Ibn Mardawayh narrated the same from him, with more detail than this.

Ibn Mardawayh also transmitted it through another route from him, in a shorter form. Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted it from him in abridged form, with the wording: he said: "He forbade his concubine, and this was made the occasion of revelation," in all the narrations that were reported from him by these chains. Al-Haytham ibn Kulayb in his Musnad, and al-Diya' al-Maqdisi in al-Mukhtarah, transmitted from the route of Nafi', from Ibn Umar, who said: "The Prophet (ﷺ) said to Hafsah: 'Do not tell anyone, and Umm Ibrahim is forbidden to me.' She said: 'Are you forbidding what God has made lawful for you?' He said: 'By God, I will not go near her.' So he did not go near her until she informed Aishah, and God revealed: ﴿God has already ordained for you the dissolving of your oaths﴾." Al-Tabarani in al-Awsat and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Abu Hurayrah that the occasion of revelation of the verse was the forbidding of Mariyah, as has passed, and its chain is weak.

These are two authentic occasions of revelation for the verse, and reconciling them is possible by the occurrence of the two incidents: the incident of the honey and the incident of Mariyah, and that the Qur'an was revealed concerning both of them together. In each of them, he confided a matter to some of his wives. As for what has been said, that the occasion was the forbidding of the woman who gave herself in marriage to the Prophet, there is nothing for it except what Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn Abbas, who said: "This verse ﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you?﴾ was revealed concerning the woman who gave herself to the Prophet (ﷺ)."

Al-Suyuti said: "Its chain is weak."

What also refutes this is that the Prophet (ﷺ) did not accept that woman who gave herself to him. How then can it be said that it was revealed concerning her: ﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you?﴾? For one who rejects what was given to him cannot properly be said to have forbidden it upon himself. Also, the words of God ﴿And when the Prophet confided a matter to one of his wives, a saying﴾ up to the end of what God related do not apply to this occasion.

As for what is established in the two Sahihs (al-Sahihayn, i.e., Bukhari and Muslim) and others, that Ibn Abbas asked Umar ibn al-Khattab about the two women who conspired against the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and he informed him that they were Aishah and Hafsah, then he mentioned the story of the ila' (oath of abstention from wives) as in the long hadith, there is nothing in this that negates that the occasion was what we mentioned earlier: the story of the honey and the story of the concubine. This is because he only informed him of the two women who conspired, and he mentioned in it that the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) (p-1507) used to argue with him, and one of them would shun him from morning until night, and that this was the reason for the seclusion, not the occasion of revelation of ﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you?﴾.

This is supported by what we mentioned earlier from Ibn Abbas, that he said to Umar: "Who are the two women who conspired?" He informed him that they were Hafsah and Aishah, and he explained to him that the occasion was the story of Mariyah.

This is what was easy to summarize regarding the occasion of revelation of the verse and the removal of the disagreement about it. So hold firmly to it, that you may be saved thereby from the confusion and mixing-up into which the commentators fell.

Abd al-Razzaq, al-Bukhari, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn Abbas that he said concerning the prohibition (haram): it requires expiation, and he said: ﴿Indeed, you have in the Messenger of God an excellent example﴾.

Ibn al-Mundhir, al-Tabarani, al-Hakim, and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from him that a man came to him and said: "I have made my wife forbidden to me." He said: "You have lied; she is not forbidden to you." Then he recited ﴿Why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you?﴾ and said: "The most stringent of the expiations for you is freeing a slave."

Al-Harith ibn Abi Usamah transmitted from Aishah that she said: "When Abu Bakr swore that he would not spend on Mistah, God revealed ﴿God has already ordained for you the dissolving of your oaths﴾, so he dissolved his oath and spent on him."

Ibn Adi and Ibn Asakir transmitted from Aishah concerning His words: ﴿And when the Prophet confided a matter to one of his wives, a saying﴾, she said: "He confided to her that Abu Bakr is my successor after me."

Ibn Adi, Abu Nu'aym in al-Sahabah, al-Ushari in Fada'il al-Siddiq, Ibn Mardawayh, and Ibn Asakir transmitted through routes from Ali and Ibn Abbas, who said: "By God, the governance of Abu Bakr and Umar is in the Book: ﴿And when the Prophet confided a matter to one of his wives, a saying﴾. He said to Hafsah: 'Your father and the father of Aishah will govern the people after me, so beware of informing anyone of this.'"

I say: this does not state that it was the occasion of revelation of His words ﴿O Prophet, why do you forbid what God has made lawful for you?﴾. Rather, it states that the matter which the Messenger of God (ﷺ) confided was this.

Even if it were granted that it has a chain fit to be considered, it is opposed by those authentic narrations that have preceded it, and those are given precedence over it and are preferred to it.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn Abbas concerning His words ﴿Your hearts have certainly swerved﴾, he said: "they deviated and sinned."

Ibn al-Mundhir transmitted from him that he said: "they inclined."

Ibn Asakir transmitted through the route of Abd Allah ibn Buraydah, from his father, concerning His words ﴿and the righteous among the believers﴾, that he said: "Abu Bakr and Umar."

Ibn Asakir transmitted from Ibn Mas'ud something similar.

Al-Tabarani, Ibn Mardawayh, and Abu Nu'aym in Fada'il al-Sahabah transmitted through another route from him something similar.

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Ibn Umar and Ibn Abbas something similar.

Al-Hakim transmitted from Abu Umamah, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ), something similar.

Ibn Abi Hatim transmitted, al-Suyuti said with a weak chain, from Ali, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ), that he said: "It is Ali ibn Abi Talib."

Ibn Mardawayh transmitted "from Asma' bint Umays: I heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: ﴿and the righteous among the believers﴾ is Ali ibn Abi Talib."

Ibn Mardawayh and Ibn Asakir transmitted from Ibn Abbas concerning His words ﴿and the righteous among the believers﴾ that he said: "It is Ali ibn Abi Talib."

Al-Tabarani and Ibn Mardawayh transmitted from Buraydah concerning His words ﴿previously married and virgins﴾, that he said: "God promised His Prophet (ﷺ) in this verse that He would marry him to the previously married Asiyah, the wife of Pharaoh, and to the virgin Maryam bint Imran."

O you who believe, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is people and stones. Protect yourselves by doing what He has commanded you and avoiding what He has forbidden, and protect your families by ordering them to obey Allah and forbidding them from His acts of disobedience. ﴿Fire whose fuel is people and stones﴾ means: a great Fire that blazes with people and with stones, just as other fires blaze with firewood. The explanation of this has already been given in Surat al-Baqarah.

Muqatil ibn Sulayman said: The meaning is: protect yourselves and your families with good discipline from the Fire in the Hereafter.

Qatadah and Mujahid said: Protect yourselves through your deeds, and protect your families through your counsel to them.

Ibn Jarir (al-Tabari) said: It is incumbent upon us to teach our children religion, goodness, and the discipline that they cannot do without. From this is His saying: ﴿Enjoin prayer upon your family and be steadfast in it﴾ [Ta-Ha: 132], and His saying: ﴿Warn your closest kindred﴾ [al-Shu'ara': 214].

﴿Over it are angels, stern and severe﴾ means: over the Fire are guardians from among the angels who are in charge of it and of punishing its people, stern toward the people of the Fire and severe toward them, not showing them mercy when they ask for mercy. This is because Allah, glorified is He, created them from His wrath and made the punishment of His creation beloved to them. It was also said: the intended meaning is stern of heart and strong of body. It was also said: stern in speech and severe in action. It was also said: the stern (ghilaz) are large of body, and the severe (shidad) are powerful.

﴿They do not disobey Allah in what He commands them﴾ means: they do not oppose Him in His command. The word ﴿ما﴾ (ma) in ﴿ما أمرهم﴾ may be a relative pronoun (mawsulah), in which case the returning pronoun is omitted, meaning: they do not disobey Allah who commanded them with it. It may also be a verbal-noun particle (masdariyyah, which turns the following verb into a verbal noun), meaning: they do not disobey Allah's command. In that case ﴿ما أمرهم﴾ would be a substitution of inclusion (badal ishtimal, where the substitute includes the meaning of the original noun) for the noun ﴿الله﴾, or it may be taken as the omission of the preposition (naz' al-khafid), meaning: they do not disobey Allah in His command. ﴿And they do what they are commanded﴾ means: they carry it out at its time without delay, neither postponing it nor bringing it forward.

﴿O you who disbelieve, do not make excuses today﴾ means: this is said to them when they are being admitted into the Fire, to despair them and to cut off their hopes. ﴿You are only being recompensed for what you used to do﴾ means: the deeds you performed in the worldly life. A similar verse is His saying: ﴿On that Day, their excuses will not benefit those who did wrong, nor will they be allowed to make amends﴾ [al-Rum: 57].

﴿O you who believe, repent to Allah with sincere repentance﴾ means: a repentance that advises its doer to abandon returning to what he has repented from. It is described this way by metaphorical attribution (al-isnad al-majazi, attributing to a thing a quality that properly belongs to its agent). Originally, the one who repents is the one who should advise himself through repentance, by resolving to abandon the sin and not to return to it.

Repentance is an individual obligation (fard 'ala al-a'yan).

Qatadah said: sincere repentance (al-tawbah al-nasuh) is truthful repentance. It was also said: it is pure repentance.

Al-Hasan said: sincere repentance is that a person hates the sin he once loved and seeks forgiveness for it whenever he remembers it.

Al-Kalbi said: sincere repentance is regret in the heart, seeking forgiveness with the tongue, withdrawing with the body, and resolving not to return to it.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it is accepted repentance.

The majority recited ﴿نصوحا﴾ (nasuhan) with a fatha on the nun, as a description of ﴿توبة﴾ (tawbah), meaning: a repentance that is thorough in sincere advice. Al-Hasan, Kharijah, and Abu Bakr (on the authority of 'Asim) recited it with a damma on the nun, meaning: a repentance that is sincere toward your own selves. It may also be the plural of nasih (sincere advisor), or it may be a verbal noun: one says nasaha nasahah wa nusuhan.

Al-Mubarrad said: He meant a repentance possessing sincere advice.

﴿It may be that your Lord will remove from you your misdeeds and admit you into gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾ means: because of that repentance. The word ﴿عسى﴾ (\'asa, "it may be") originally expresses hope, but when it comes from Allah it is binding, because the one who repents from sin is like one who has no sin. The word ﴿يدخلكم﴾ (yudkhilakum) is conjoined to ﴿يكفر﴾ (yukaffir) and is in the accusative case by the particle governing it. The majority recited it in the accusative. It was also recited in the jussive, as a conjunction to the place (mahall) of ﴿عسى﴾, as if He had said: Repent, and that will require the removal of your misdeeds and will admit you.

﴿On the Day when Allah will not disgrace the Prophet﴾: the adverbial phrase ﴿يوم﴾ (yawm) is connected to ﴿يدخلكم﴾, meaning: He will admit you on the Day when Allah will not disgrace the Prophet. ﴿And those who believed with him﴾: the relative phrase is conjoined to ﴿النبي﴾ (the Prophet). It was also said that the relative phrase is a subject whose predicate is ﴿نورهم يسعى بين أيديهم وبأيمانهم﴾ (their light runs before them and on their right). The first view is preferable, and the clause ﴿نورهم يسعى﴾ is either in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause (hal) or is a resumed clause explaining their state. It has already been mentioned in Surat al-Hadid that their light will be with them while they walk upon the Sirat (bridge over Hell). The clause ﴿يقولون ربنا أتمم لنا نورنا واغفر لنا إنك على كل شيء قدير﴾ (They say: Our Lord, perfect our light for us and forgive us; indeed You are over all things competent) is also in the accusative position as a circumstantial clause. Originally, the one who repents is the one who should advise himself through repentance, by resolving to abandon the sin and not to return to it.

Repentance is an individual obligation (fard 'ala al-a'yan).

Qatadah said: sincere repentance (al-tawbah al-nasuh) is truthful repentance. It was also said: it is pure repentance.

Al-Hasan said: sincere repentance is that a person hates the sin he once loved and seeks forgiveness for it whenever he remembers it.

Al-Kalbi said: sincere repentance is regret in the heart, seeking forgiveness with the tongue, withdrawing with the body, and resolving not to return to it.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: it is accepted repentance.

Al-Mubarrad said: He meant a repentance possessing sincere advice.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 66, verses 9–12:

His saying: ﴿O Prophet, strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites﴾, that is, with the sword and with argument. The discussion of this verse has already passed in Surat Bara'a. ﴿And be harsh with them﴾, that is, be severe with them in the call, and employ roughness in enjoining upon them the sharia.

Al-Hasan (may Allah have mercy on him) said: that is, strive against them by enforcing the prescribed punishments (hudud) upon them, for they were committing the things that require the hudud. ﴿Their refuge is Hell﴾, that is, their destination is to it, meaning the disbelievers and the hypocrites. ﴿And wretched is the destination﴾, that is, the place to which they return.

﴿Allah presents an example for those who disbelieve: the wife of Noah and the wife of Lot﴾. It has been mentioned more than once that "example" (mathal) may mean presenting a strange situation by which another situation similar to it in strangeness is recognized. That is, Allah made an example of the condition of these disbelievers, and that no one avails anyone else. ﴿The wife of Noah and the wife of Lot﴾: this is the first object, and "example" (mathalan) is the second object, as we have already established its verification. It was postponed so that what explains it and clarifies its meaning would be joined to it. ﴿They were under two of Our righteous servants﴾, and they are Noah and Lot, that is, they were in the bond of their marriage. ﴿But they betrayed them﴾, that is, betrayal occurred from them toward them.

Ikrimah and al-Dahhak said: by disbelief. It was also said: the wife of Noah used to tell people that he was mad, and the wife of Lot used to inform her people about his guests. It is agreed upon that the wife of a prophet never committed adultery at all.

It was also said: their betrayal was hypocrisy.

It was also said: they betrayed them by tale-bearing. ﴿So they did not avail them against Allah at all﴾, that is, Noah and Lot did not benefit them in any benefit by reason of their being their wives, nor did they ward off from them any of Allah's punishment by their honour before Allah. ﴿And it was said: Enter the Fire with those who enter﴾, that is, it was said to them in the Hereafter, or at the time of their death: enter the Fire with those who enter it of the people of disbelief and sins.

Yahya ibn Sallam said: Allah made an example for those who disbelieve, warning thereby Aisha and Hafsa against opposing the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) when they both colluded against him.

How well said the one who said: the mention of the wives of the two prophets after the mention of their story and their collusion against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) guides in the most complete guidance and alludes in the most eloquent allusion that the intent is to frighten them together with the rest of the Mothers of the Believers, and clarifies that although they were under the bond of the best of Allah's creation and the seal of His messengers, that does not avail them against Allah at all. Allah has preserved them from the sin of that collusion by the sincere and pure repentance that occurred from them.

﴿And Allah presents an example for those who believe: the wife of Pharaoh﴾. The discussion of this is like the discussion of the example before it, that is, Allah made the condition of Pharaoh's wife an example for the condition of the believers, as encouragement for them to remain steadfast in obedience, to hold fast to the religion, and to be patient in hardship, and that the assault of disbelief does not harm them, just as it did not harm Pharaoh's wife. She was under the most disbelieving of the disbelievers, yet by her faith in Allah she came to be in the Gardens of Bliss. ﴿When she said: My Lord, build for me a house with You in Paradise﴾. The adverbial phrase (idh) is related either to "daraba" or to "mathalan": that is, build for me a house near Your mercy, or in the highest ranks of those brought near to You, or in a place where none acts except by Your permission, which is Paradise. ﴿And save me from Pharaoh and his deeds﴾, that is, from his person and the evil deeds that proceed from him. ﴿And save me from the wrongdoing people﴾. Al-Kalbi said: they are the people of Egypt.

Muqatil said: they are the Copts.

Al-Hasan and Ibn Kaysan said: Allah saved her with the noblest salvation and raised her to Paradise, where she eats and drinks.

﴿And Mary daughter of Imran, who guarded her chastity﴾. It is conjoined to "the wife of Pharaoh", that is, and Allah presented as an example for those who believe Mary daughter of Imran, that is, her condition and attribute. It was also said that the governing element for Mary is an implied verb, that is, "and mention Mary". The purpose of mentioning her is that Allah, glory be to Him, combined for her the honour of this world and the Hereafter, and chose her over the women of the worlds, despite being among a disbelieving people. ﴿Who guarded her chastity﴾, that is, from immoralities. The explanation of this has already passed in Surat an-Nisa.

The exegetes said: what is meant by "farj" here is the collar (jayb), due to His saying: ﴿So We breathed into it of Our Spirit﴾, for Gabriel breathed into the collar of her garment, and she conceived Jesus. ﴿And she affirmed the words of her Lord﴾, meaning His laws which He prescribed for His servants. It was also said: what is meant by "the words" here is Gabriel's saying to her: ﴿I am only the messenger of your Lord﴾ [Maryam: 19], and so on.

Muqatil said: by "the words" he means Jesus.

The majority read ﴿wa-saddaqat﴾ with shaddah, while Hamzah al-Umawi, Ya'qub, Qatadah, Abu Mijlaz, and 'Asim in one narration from him read it without shaddah.

The majority read "bi-kalimat" in the plural, while al-Hasan, Mujahid, and al-Jahdari read "bi-kalimah" in the singular.

The majority read "wa-kitabihi" in the singular, while the people of Basra and Hafs read "wa-kutubihi" in the plural. The intended meaning according to the reading of the majority is the genus, so it carries the sense of the plural, namely the books revealed to the prophets. ﴿And she was of the devout (qanitin)﴾. Qatadah said: of the people obedient to their Lord.

'Ata' said: of those who pray; she used to pray between Maghrib and 'Isha'. It is also permissible that by "qanitin" is meant her kin and clan from whom she came, who were obedient, a household of righteousness and obedience. He said "min al-qanitin" and did not say "min al-qanitat", giving precedence to the masculine over the feminine.

In the two Sahihs and elsewhere, from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari from the Prophet (ﷺ), he said: "Many men have reached perfection, but none among women has reached perfection except Asiyah the wife of Pharaoh, Mary daughter of 'Imran, and Khadijah daughter of Khuwaylid. And the superiority of 'Aishah over women is like the superiority of tharid over the rest of food."

Waki' related in al-Gharar from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿And save me from Pharaoh and his deeds﴾, that he said: from his community.
